title: Source errata
$comment:
Authored corrections to DEFECTIVE SOURCE LINES, one entry per line. This file exists so that a one-off scorer error never becomes a reason to weaken a general rule. Every rule in the parser is scored corpus-wide against cases whose answer is already known; a phenomenon with N=1 cannot be scored that way, and a rule written to swallow it is a hardcode wearing a rule's clothes. Errata are the pressure valve that keeps the general rules general.

An erratum is admissible only when BOTH hold: the phenomenon is essentially unique in the corpus (N=1 or 2), AND other evidence in the same game FORCES the correction -- the batting order, the boxscore line, the linescore, an inning summary. `evidence` must name it. An erratum is not a place to record an opinion about what a line probably meant.

Corrections apply to the raw PBP line text before the grammar sees it, so the corrected line is parsed by exactly the same rules as every other line -- there is no erratum code path through the parser. Each application is disclosed in the game file's `inferred[]` under rule `erratum`, so a consumer that wants only what the source said can drop the events it names.

erratum_id.description: Stable identifier, `<game_id>-<n>`, unique across this file.

raw_sha256.description: sha256 of the VERBATIM source line this erratum was authored against, whitespace included. The loader refuses to apply an erratum whose line no longer hashes to this, so a change in the source detaches the correction LOUDLY instead of silently rewriting different text.

raw_excerpt.description: The defective line, whitespace collapsed. For human review only -- `raw_sha256` is what the loader matches on.

replace.description: Substring of the raw line to replace. Must occur EXACTLY ONCE in it; the loader refuses a substring that is absent or ambiguous.

class.description: What kind of defect the SOURCE has. Not a parser concept -- these describe the scorer's error. `inflated_inning_summary_lob` is the one entry here that is a POPULATION rather than a one-off: an Inning Summary whose LOB exceeds the runners its own half actually left on base, by exactly one. See bc_pipeline.errata for why a population belongs here anyway.

evidence.description: What FORCES this correction, stated so a reader can check it without rerunning anything. Name the batting-order positions, the box columns, the linescore cells. 'Looks wrong' is not evidence.
